text: In this world, everyone has a number above their head.
It shows how many people really like you.
You see, you can't fake it. And family doesn't count.
Pop stars have millions.
My dog has six.
And Grandma? Four hundred. She bakes cookies.
Me? I have exactly one.
Kids call me Lonely One.
I always figured my one was the lunch lady.
Then one day, Brayden, nine hundred likes, laughed in my face.
Bet you can't hit ten by Friday.
speaker: brayden

text: So I tried everything.
Free candy. Still one.
A backflip... onto the teacher. Still one.
Friday. School dance. My number? One.
Subscribe, because that's when everything went wrong.
Brayden slipped on stage. His pants ripped. Everyone laughed.
His number started falling. Nine hundred. Two hundred. Ten.
That's when I realized something.
Likes aren't something you get. They're something you give.
So I walked up, tied my hoodie around his waist, and said, nice moves, man.
Ding. Ding. Ding. Two. Twenty. Fifty!
But nobody was looking at my number.
They were looking at Lily, the quiet girl in the back.
Her number was one too.
My one was never the lunch lady. It was her.
And her one... was me.
Subscribe if you've got a one.
